reviews.reason: The canonical DOC reader implements the Word 97+ profile; a retained table stream cannot make an older nFib layout supported.
reviews.required_evidence: Precise older-profile refusal before modern pointer interpretation, independent of table-stream presence and stylesheet leniency, while retaining the known Word 97 compatibility exceptions.
reviews.observed_evidence: Five older nFib values on two native-source derivatives now return exact UnsupportedVersion values/names under both leniency modes, rather than a misleading CLX-corruption error. The positional edit owner returns UnsupportedSource. Word 6/95 derivatives propagate UnsupportedFormat through both public operations ingress routes. C0/C2 variants retain text, pointer count, template flag and no-op bytes.
reviews.supported_scope: Word 97+ canonical reads and the existing C0 shell/C2 bidi compatibility admission within the implemented profile. Low-level FIB inspection remains separate from document admission.
reviews.unsupported_scope: Reading Word 6/95 and earlier incompatible layouts as modern DOC, including attempts to use modern Table streams to bypass the profile boundary. No complete early Word implementation or legacy application compatibility is supplied.
reviews.scope_limit: Native-source incompatible-header derivatives and an explicit library profile limit, not native-authored legacy specimens or positive coverage of legacy reading. Historical status and original fixtures are unchanged.

reviews.reason: Cryptographic signature validity, payload integrity, signature-presence/edit policy and PKI trust are distinct contracts. The shared verifier deliberately does not perform ambient certificate trust or revocation lookup.
reviews.required_evidence: Explicit Trust::NotChecked alongside valid signature/integrity reports, invalid-payload separation, and evidence that a nonempty certificate list does not silently become trusted.
reviews.observed_evidence: Caller-key signature derivatives over native Office parents verify supported-resource integrity and mathematical signatures while reporting Trust::NotChecked. Native workbook derivatives also verify explicit unsign policy and distinguish payload tampering from valid signature math. The pre-existing tracked Microsoft Office 2010 signed DOCX/XLSX/PPTX fixtures contain certificates and verify under their compatible SHA-1 policy, yet now explicitly assert Trust::NotChecked; these supplemental files are separate from the 139-file corpus.
reviews.supported_scope: Bounded mathematical integrity/signature verification, explicit complete/partial coverage reports, certificate metadata, and supported signature presence/consumption policy. Native parent data remains inert and preserved.
reviews.unsupported_scope: Certificate-chain trust, revocation, signer authority, organizational trust policy, ambient credential/provider lookup and native Office acceptance. A Signed wrapper detects presence rather than proving validity or trust.
reviews.scope_limit: An explicit trust boundary, not positive semantic coverage of PKI or a new native signed specimen. Generated signatures use disposable local keys; native-authored signature handoffs remain distinct. No trust lookup, revocation request or fresh native application validation is performed.
